summary: A strict modular grid, Helvetica, flush-left ragged-right text, and objective photography. Nothing decorative survives.
source: Looka §6 · Tilda Swiss Style · UX Planet §49 · International Typographic Style (Müller-Brockmann, Keller, Hofmann)

ink.role: pure black — this pack is one of the few that earns it

red.role: THE one flag red. There is no second accent

grid.note: or a modular grid (columns x rows) for poster layouts

type.rule: tracking sign FLIPS between display and body. Getting it backwards is the commonest Swiss mistake.

focus.reason: the one place the flag red does double duty. Red on white is 4.3:1 — above the 3:1 that 2.4.13 requires for a state change, and unmistakable against a black-and-white page.

motion.note: no easing. Swiss is objective and precise; a transition is neither.

copyBudget.headlineReason: display runs 44-96px; six words is already three lines
copyBudget.note: size CONTRAST is the style's core move — a large heading against small body. Tilda states it explicitly.

a11y.note: the easiest pack in the catalogue to make accessible: pure black on pure white is 21:1, and there is no depth system to get wrong.
a11y.targetSizeNote: Small uppercase meta links are the pack's target-size risk: 12px with no padding is 13.33px tall, well under 24x24. Nav links carry min-height:24px. Caught by the self-audit.

banned: justified text — ragged right is doctrine

darkMode.note: Inverts to pure black ground with white type. The red stays #e2231a — on black it is 4.9:1, slightly better than on white. Photography must be re-graded or it floats.

scroll.headline: scroll-progress (●)
scroll.reason: a solid red bar, 4-8px, is straight out of the poster vocabulary. It is also the cheapest technique in the catalogue and survives reduced motion, because a progress indicator conveys position (WCAG 2.3.3 exempts it).
banned: parallax — layers moving independently place elements off-grid on every frame
smooth-scroll — Swiss is objective and precise; inertia is neither

sheet.metaLine: 12-col grid · Helvetica 700/-.03em display · one flag red · radius 0
tokenTable: or a modular grid for poster layouts

notes.tokens: The grid is not a metaphor — it is a literal, visible, countable structure. Set the grid first, place type into it flush left, then let images occupy whole cells. Asymmetry comes from which cells you leave empty, not from nudging things off-grid.
notes.nav: A rule and a row of labels. No bar, no fill, no radius. The active item is marked by weight, not by a pill — a pill would be a rounded container in a pack that bans radius.
notes.hero: Size contrast is the whole move. Tilda states it directly: large headings against small body text. A 46px display over 12px meta is more Swiss than any amount of grid.
notes.button: A black box that inverts on hover. No transition — Swiss is objective and precise; easing is neither. Focus is the one place the flag red does double duty, at 4.3:1 on white.
notes.form: A field is a box with a 2px rule under it. The error is a red rule plus text — red alone would be colour-only signalling, and this pack has exactly one red to spend.
notes.card: There is no card. Content occupies grid cells. The specimen shows cells with a top rule, which is the closest this pack comes to a container.
notes.table: Swiss at its most natural — this is what the style was built for. Column heads at 11px +.02em uppercase, rules at 2px, everything flush left.
notes.overlay: A flat black scrim and a white panel with a red rule. No radius, no shadow, no blur. The panel is identified by the rule, not by elevation.
notes.empty: A red rule, a statement, one action. The pack has no dashed-border vocabulary — a dashed line is decorative, so absence is signalled by the red rule instead.
notes.dark: Inverts to pure black. The red stays #e2231a and is actually better on black (4.9:1) than on white (4.3:1). Photography must be re-graded or objective colour images float on a black ground.
notes.narrow: 12 columns collapse to 4, then to 1 — but the grid stays visible. A Swiss page that becomes a centred single column at mobile has stopped being Swiss.
notes.copy: The only pack here that keeps the engine's 420 chars per viewport, because dense small body text against huge display type is the style.

Display and body one step apart, so the size contrast that defines the style has gone, and the paragraph runs uncapped across the full container width with no measure, which is the failure WCAG 1.4.8 exists to prevent and which Swiss avoids by construction.
